rites.name: Karouzhok
rites.text: Karouzhok is the concept of Sestia's Seeding, the stretch of time when the makers set the Weave into the ground and the sleeping powers of the world are gently woken and then hushed again. It is less a thing than a promise that the quiet of creation can be bent toward growth.

rites.name: Oriasor
rites.text: Oriasor is the concept of the Weave as the Sestian makers planted it in the Seeding, a latent lattice of quiet powers that wait beneath the world. In the Holy Age its flame-bearing orders learned to wake only fragments of it, and the sleeping current was never fully spent.

rites.name: Silamennae
rites.text: Silamennae is the concept of the Sestian grove-gardens, the living seed-stores that the first sovereign tended through the Fall and the Sundering. It was the root of the Pact, the bond by which the broken shards agreed to share their growth. In the Age of the first sovereign it still shapes how the groves and kingdoms regard one another.

rites.name: Silamys
rites.text: Silamys is the concept of binding oaths as they were taken during the Sundering, when the old worlds split and the Pact was first sworn among the orders of the Holy Age. It is remembered as the force that held a promise together while the ground of the Shards cracked beneath it.

rites.name: Voroktoukar
rites.text: Voroktoukar is the Sestian concept of the wall that holds back the tide of the unmade, raised in the Walled Age and kept by the orders who swore their lives to its mending. Its churches teach that every crossing of the wall is paid for in a single human name, which is why the first crossings are still remembered as ledgers of loss.

rites.name: Sereollesia
rites.text: Sereollesia is the luminous wayfinder of the Sestian tides, a bright ember said to ride the upper air and lead voyagers across the open dark. Her presence is felt as a sudden streak of silver that marks the course home for those who keep faith with the swell.

rites.name: Coraurnus
rites.text: Coraurnus is the tide-bound war-spirit of Sestia's scattered reef-isles, a concept rather than a figure, woven into the oaths sworn before every sea-raid. Its power wakes only when shorelines are contested, and it is said to sink fleets by pulling the sea itself into a single restless rage.

rites.name: Ventor
rites.text: Ventor is a concept-born wind-spirit of the Sestian mythic era, said to be woven from the breath that crosses the edges of the Lantern Sea. It is less a being than a recurring weather of the mind, appearing wherever a sailor's courage turns into a squall.

rites.name: Nuilamwen
rites.text: Nuilamwen is the concept of the branching ending, a pattern the Library of Sestia uses to shelve every future that has not yet settled into one. In the Age of the first sovereign, groves and growing kingdoms take their shape from which of those branches is being held open.

rites.name: Anakamoma
rites.text: Anakamoma is the concept of a branching ending, the moment in Sestia's Three Futures when a single thread splits into shelved outcomes within the Library. It is said to hold the weight of every unchosen ending, and during the Age of Sundering its pull was felt wherever landfall broke the old bonds between peoples.
